# `ota_prepare_module`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Updater (firmware 9.75): prepare the device to receive one module package on the binary socket.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ (firmware 9.75); partly INFERRED, see description |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.75, updater RPC handler @0x27710 (64-bit build), OTA manager; app 3.3.2 OtaService DTOs |

Firmware 9.75 (app 3.4.0) registers this method in the updater on TCP 4350, in both the 64-bit and 32-bit builds; firmware 9.31 registered none of the OTA methods (its updater had four). The handler clears the thread error code and calls the updater's single OTA manager. The OTA methods do not use the imager/guider secure-session layer (no such code in the updater); whether the JSON on 4350 is wrapped is not established. Firmware update is a high-risk operation; do not send this to a real device to test it. Prepares reception of one module package, named in send_modules. The device creates a partial file for the package, arms the binary receiver for the caller's address, and replies with the module's size and SHA-256 from the target manifest, the binary port and whether the module was already received (the client then skips it). The reply carries binary_port, but the app ignores it and always streams to TCP 4361. After the reply the client streams the package file raw on 4361 with no header. When the stream ends the device checks the byte count (error 525 on mismatch) and the SHA-256 (also 525), then renames the partial file to the final package name (515 on failure). It emits an OtaUpdate event with state working at prepare time and again as the stage changes. If no ota_prepare_module arrives within the pending timeout (15 s, see ota_begin) the session fails. Unlike the legacy begin_recv (which needs the caller's 4361 connection to exist first), this path uses a pending-receive record keyed by the caller's address and a pending timeout, so the 4361 connection need not exist at prepare time; the exact ordering rules are INFERRED. If the binary connection does not arrive within 15 s of the prepare reply (a 15000 ms comparison on the pending-receive start time, checked once per loop of the updater network thread, whose select timeout is 5 s, so it fires within about 5 s after the 15 s mark) the device clears the pending record and fails the receive with code 546 and the text ota module binary connection timeout (firmware 9.75, 64-bit build, READ; new in 9.75; the 32-bit build has the check but its constants were not located).

Side effects: Creates a partial package file and arms the binary receiver.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"ota_prepare_module"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | no | - | Object params with name. A missing or non-string name gives 105. [READ] |
| `params.name` | string | yes | - | Module name from send_modules. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (error) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 105 | params.name missing or not a string | `invalid name` |
| 107 | Missing params | `missing params` |
| 102 | Module not in target_manifest or not in send_modules | `invalid module` |
| 546 | The binary connection did not arrive within 15 s of the prepare reply. Reported through the OtaUpdate failure event and the session failure, not in this reply (firmware 9.75, 64-bit build) | `ota module binary connection timeout` |
| 524 | Stage conflict or busy: the call is not allowed in the current OTA stage (text names the stage and, where relevant, asks the caller to ota_abort first) | `stage conflict` |

## Example

Request, request - Shape READ; all values invented:

```json
{"id":100,"method":"ota_prepare_module","params":{"name":"example_module"}}
```

Reply, ok - Shape READ; all values invented:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"ota_prepare_module","result":{"name":"example_module","size":1048576,"sha256":"<64 hex digits>","binary_port":4361,"already_received":false},"code":0,"id":100}
```
